01 / About me

About me

My research focuses on adapting models from mathematical biology to study social issues.

I am a Ph.D. candidate in Applied Mathematics at Washington State University, advised by Dr. Sergey Lapin and Dr. Judi McDonald. My research includes modeling calls for service and opioid use disorder.

Alongside research, I teach mathematics and participate in community outreach and student organizations.

Mathematical modelingDifferential equationsStatistical analysisPythonRData visualization
02 / Research & projects

Research & projects

Selected research projects.

01

Patterns in calls for service

I analyze calls-for-service data to understand how call patterns vary over time and across agencies. My work includes building reproducible analysis pipelines, exploring daily call counts, and developing models for interactions among call categories.

Methods: exploratory data analysis · time series analysis · dynamical systems

02

Modeling opioid use disorder

I develop compartmental models to study how prevention compliance and treatment adherence affect opioid use disorder outcomes. This work uses differential equations, numerical simulations, and sensitivity analysis to examine treatment, relapse, and overdose deaths.

Methods: ordinary differential equations · equilibrium analysis · sensitivity analysis

03 / Teaching & outreach

Teaching & outreach

Teaching

At Washington State University, I have served as an instructor, lecturer, teaching assistant, and course coordinator. I have taught college algebra, pre-calculus, and mathematics for business, with experience leading both my own courses and lab sections.

As a course coordinator, I have also supported the organization and delivery of instruction across course sections.

Community outreach

Through Data Playshops, I have helped coordinate and lead more than 13 events introducing elementary students to data and mathematical thinking. I have also developed Spanish-language materials to make these activities accessible to more students and families.

I have taught through Dare to Dream, supporting students as they explore mathematics and opportunities in higher education.

As an instructor for the ESTEEMED MIRA program, I have also contributed to mathematics instruction for participating students.

Student organizations

I served as an officer in WSU’s American Mathematical Society (AMS) student chapter for three years and in the Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) student chapter for two years. Through these organizations, I have helped support activities and build community among mathematics students.
